record.original_question: Classify binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros by minimum distance and determine their weight enumerators, since the chapter says this classification had not been achieved and the weight-enumerator problem remained very difficult.

evidence.quote: This section is concerned with the classification of the codes Cr,s by means of their minimum distance. Our aim is to recall that this classification is not yet achieved; furthermore the determination of the weight enumerators ap￾pears as a most difficult problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m ≥ 2 be an integer and let n = 2^m - 1. For integers r, s with 0 ≤ r < s ≤ n-1, define the binary cyclic code C_{r,s} of length n to be the binary cyclic code whose dual has as zeros exactly the conjugates of α^r and α^s, where α is a primitive n-th root of unity in F_{2^m}; equivalently, C_{r,s} is the binary cyclic code of length n whose defining set is the union of the 2-cyclotomic cosets of r and s modulo n. Such codes are called binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros.

(a) Classify, up to equivalence, all binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros according to their minimum distance: for each pair (r, s) (or each pair of 2-cyclotomic cosets), determine d(C_{r,s}).

(b) For every such code C_{r,s}, determine its weight enumerator W_{C_{r,s}}(x, y) = Σ_{c ∈ C_{r,s}} x^{n - wt(c)} y^{wt(c)}.
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros by minimum distance, together with the determination of their weight enumerators, remains open. The literature contains only partial results: weight distributions and minimum-distance results are known for specific families (e.g., codes whose duals have two zeros analyzed via Gaussian periods, or via Hermitian forms graphs), but no complete classification or general weight-enumerator formula is available.

status_evidence.title: A family of cyclic codes with two zeros
status_evidence.snippet: Cyclic codes with two zeros and their dual codes have been a subject of study for many years, though their weight distributions are known only for a few cases.
status_evidence.claim: Weight distributions of two-zero cyclic codes are known only for a few cases, indicating the general problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Two classes of binary cyclic codes and their weight distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Two classes of cyclic codes whose duals have two zeros have been presented, with weight distributions settled using Gaussian periods.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific subfamilies have been resolved, not the general two-zero case.
